text: The chain-check Schedule decisionChainCheck lives in rwb-decision as JOB-14 at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and its ChainCheckWorkflow checks the central ledger of rwb_decision and every wave-1 local decision_record chain it has ingested, from chain_seq 1 to the highest chain_seq at the start of each chain, in batches of 1,000, recomputing every entry_hash and comparing every prev_hash. For each chain the run names the first break by service, chain and entry ID with its chain_seq, counts every failing entry, and names a local record with no ledger entry as a gap and a ledger entry with no local record as an orphan. Before it starts, the run waits for the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger to reach the producer watermark, re-reading it every 5 minutes, and it starts at 04:00 at the latest with the note ingest not at watermark; the run record names that watermark in place of the JOB-13 end time. One incident is raised with one MSG-P7-008 for the first break per chain and every gap, MSG-P7-007 carries the count and the last hash when every chain is intact, and MSG-P7-013 carries the date of the last complete check when the run stops.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 28 and 44 and the Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 14 and 16 give the local record, the topic, the central ledger and the 02:00 Schedule but never the scope of the check over the 19 local chains, the watermark that replaces the JOB-13 end time, or per-chain reporting. Without those three choices the workflow, the ingest wait and the harness cannot be built; every value in this assumption is copied from the legacy story or from the two design decks and no business value is invented.

text: The JOB-14 run record is the workflow result of ChainCheckWorkflow, read through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs and rerun through POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, both owned by P1 rwb-source-data under the Ownership Map; a rerun writes a new run record with rerun true for the same business date and changes nothing else, and the SKIP policy of the Schedule refuses a second concurrent start. The break incident, MSG-P7-007, MSG-P7-008 and MSG-P7-013 leave the rwb-decision worker through the ACE Common notification path to the Compliance and PDPA officer role RW-COMPLY, the break incident also reaches the security administrator role RW-SECADM, and a failed or stopped run alerts the platform administrator role RW-PLATADM. The harness starts the Schedule once through the Temporal client with the same input the cadence uses and never calls the workflow through another service.
why: The legacy story writes the run record to the ACE job run record and serves it through GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs on the monolith base, and it sends the reports through the ACE notification path of one service. The target has no monolith job table, the job monitor operation is owned by rwb-source-data in the Ownership Map while the check runs in rwb-decision, and no source states how the incident and the report cross the service boundary. The operations, the roles and the messages named are the ones the Ownership Map and the legacy story already publish.

text: A calling service reaches an agent run by starting AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent through the P10 contract of rwb-agent, with the rule result already built in the calling service and the 60 second policy timeout as the workflow budget; the client does not call rwb-agent by REST inside the step. When the workflow has not answered inside the 60 second budget the client treats the expiry as TIMED_OUT, applies the rule result and reads the run, its status and its fallback through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs.
why: Architecture v5 slide 16 gives rwb-agent a Temporal workflow and the legacy client called an in-process orchestrator and read runs by REST; no source states which one the client uses, and no source states how a caller gets the result when the workflow completes after the budget. Without the ruling the harness cannot assert where the 60 second budget lives, and the client contract of the calling service cannot be written.

text: rwb-decision (P7) owns authoring, the load checks, the at-least-50-scenario gate, four-eyes approval, effective dating and one-call rollback; each service that evaluates a model fetches it on RulePackageInForce, verifies the SHA-256 checksum and swaps it atomically, keeping the last good model when a load fails; the four services of the integration dependency list are the wave-1 parties this story exercises, rwb-case evaluating package ALLOCATION, rwb-comms and rwb-integration evaluating the package each is assigned, and rwb-decision governing all three; and the 50-scenario gate is the platform setting rules.testcases.min read through the parameters contract, never a value in code.

Without the reading the harness has no service to point each property at.
